cards.title: The Scramble
body: Starting trade from 1800s the slave decline and the Europeans changed another form of trade which asked permanent settlements of Europeans in Africa and this started colonialism.
In West Africa British set up colonies in West Africa in gold coast and Sierra-lone in 1874 & A
French also created the largest colonial empire in West Africa the French West Africa in 1900.In 1900 Germany established colony in Togo, Cameroon, Tanzania &Namibia.

cards.title: Past exam (Matric 2018)
cards.q: The part of Africa which had been affected more by the slave trade was ...
cards.why:
**Step 1:** From the lesson: “Starting from the 1800s the slave trade declined; West Africa had been the region most affected by it.”

**Step 2:** West Africa was the primary source for the Trans-Atlantic Slave Trade. Millions of Africans were captured from this region and transported to the Americas to work on plantations.

**Step 3:** So the answer is B) West Africa..

**Tip:** Underline the key word in the question (true / not / except / first / last), then test every option against the lesson facts and dates.

cards.title: Past exam (Matric 2017)
cards.q: One of the following countries **was not** a French colony in West Africa.
cards.why:
**Step 1:** From the lesson: “France created the largest colonial empire in West Africa, French West Africa, in 1900 (the Gambia was British).”

**Step 2:** Gambia was a British colony, surrounded almost entirely by Senegal (which was French). Senegal, Upper Volta (now Burkina Faso), Niger, and Mali were all part of French West Africa.

**Step 3:** So the answer is D) Gambia.

**Tip:** Underline the key word in the question (true / not / except / first / last), then test every option against the lesson facts and dates.

cards.title: Model answer: the Scramble for Africa
cards.problem: (Exam question) Explain how the Scramble for Africa began and give examples in West Africa.

steps.text: Change in trade: from the 1800s the slave trade declined and Europeans turned to a new trade that needed permanent European settlement – the start of colonialism.
Britain: set up colonies in the Gold Coast and Sierra Leone.
France: created the largest colonial empire in West Africa, French West Africa (1900).
Germany: Togo, Cameroon, Tanzania and Namibia.

cards.answer: As the slave trade ended, Europeans sought raw materials and markets through permanent colonies; Britain, France and Germany carved up West Africa and beyond.

cards.title: North Africa -Egypt
body: Mohammed Ali established a separate empire in Egypt in 1805 known as the Mamluk dynasty .He modernized Egypt.
In 1854 the project of opening Suez Canal was started by French engineer Ferdinand de lespese and ended in 1869.
As the gate to three continents Suez Canal became strategically important and Britain bought share in 1875.
The Egyptians revolted in 1881 hating the European dominance, but it was crushed but Britain and Egypt became British protectorate in 1914.
Sudan became independent by the Mahdi revolution led by clerk Mohammed Ahmad in 1881 but British crush the revolution and Sudan became its colony.
Algeria starting from 1872 became French settler colony, soon France made morocco and Tunisia under her protectorate in 1912.
In north east Africa Italy set up colony in Eritrea and Somali but defeated in attempt to control Ethiopia in 1896.

cards.title: Past exam (Model exam 2015)
cards.q: The following were British colonies in Africa **except**:
cards.why:
**Step 1:** From the lesson: “Algeria starting from 1872 became French settler colony, soon France made morocco and Tunisia under her protectorate in 1912.”

**Step 2:** **Tunisia** was a French protectorate (colony), not British. Nigeria, Kenya, Uganda, and Zimbabwe (Southern Rhodesia) were all part of the British Empire in Africa.

**Step 3:** So the answer is D) Tunisia.

**Tip:** Underline the key word in the question (true / not / except / first / last), then test every option against the lesson facts and dates.

cards.title: Past exam (Model exam 2023)
cards.q: Before Suez Canal was Nationalized by Gamal Abdel Nasser, it owned and operated by the joint administration of ...
cards.why:
**Step 1:** From the lesson: “In 1854 the project of opening the Suez Canal was started by the French engineer Ferdinand de Lesseps and ended in 1869; Britain bought shares in 1875.”

**Step 2:** The Suez Canal Company was primarily owned by **British and French** shareholders. Nasser's nationalization of the canal in 1956 led to a military intervention by Britain, France, and Israel.

**Step 3:** So the answer is B) Britain and France..

**Tip:** Underline the key word in the question (true / not / except / first / last), then test every option against the lesson facts and dates.

cards.title: Model answer: North Africa under colonialism
cards.problem: (Exam question) Describe how European powers took control of North Africa.

steps.text: Egypt: Mohammed Ali modernised Egypt from 1805; the Suez Canal (1854–1869) became strategically vital and Britain bought shares in 1875; the 1881 revolt was crushed and Egypt became a British protectorate in 1914.
Sudan: the Mahdist revolution of 1881 was crushed by Britain, which made Sudan a colony.
French North Africa: Algeria became a French settler colony; Morocco and Tunisia became French protectorates in 1912.
North-east Africa: Italy took Eritrea and Somalia but was defeated in Ethiopia in 1896.

cards.answer: Britain took Egypt and Sudan, France took Algeria, Tunisia and Morocco, and Italy took Eritrea and Somalia – driven by the strategic Suez Canal and imperial rivalry.

cards.title: Central Africa
body: Central Africa became famous after the coming of the famous explorer David Livingstone in 1800s.

After his death henry Stanly continued his legacy and asked British for help but British refused. King Leopold 2ND of Belgium accepted him and he crated the largest colonial empire in central Africa .soon France also established colony here.

cards.problem: (Short answer) How was Central Africa colonised?

steps.text: Exploration: David Livingstone made the region famous in the 1800s.
Stanley: after Livingstone's death Henry Stanley continued his work and asked Britain for help, but Britain refused.
Belgium: King Leopold II accepted Stanley and created the largest colonial empire in Central Africa (the Congo).

cards.answer: Explorers Livingstone and Stanley opened the region; Leopold II of Belgium built the largest Central African empire, with France also taking territory.

cards.title: East Africa
body: In east Africa British and Germany rivaled for colonies .and agreed by the berlin conference .British took Kenya and Germany Tanzania and Zanzibar, Mozambique to Portugal and Rwanda to Belgium.

The Berlin Conference was conducted between 1884-85 in Germany to stop any conflicts between Europeans in Africa. The were asked just to register their colony between Berlin office to get recognition.

cards.title: Past exam (Model exam 2016)

options.A: specify the conditions for African colonialism

cards.why:
**Step 1:** The **Berlin Conference** (1884–1885) was organized to regulate European colonization and trade in Africa. It established the principle of 'effective occupation,' which specified the conditions European powers had to meet to claim African territories.

**Step 2:** So the answer is A) specify the conditions for African colonialism.

**Tip:** Underline the key word in the question (true / not / except / first / last), then test every option against the lesson facts and dates.

cards.title: Past exam (Model exam 2022)
cards.q: One of the following states was **not** British former colony:
cards.why:
**Step 1:** From the lesson: “In east Africa British and Germany rivaled for colonies: Britain took Kenya, Germany took Tanzania, Mozambique went to Portugal and Rwanda to Belgium.”

**Step 2:** **Historical Fact:** 
- Kenya, Nigeria, and Uganda were British colonies.
- **Rwanda** was originally a German colony (part of German East Africa) and later became a Belgian trust territory after WWI. It was never a British colony.

**Step 3:** So the answer is C) Rwanda.

**Tip:** Underline the key word in the question (true / not / except / first / last), then test every option against the lesson facts and dates.

cards.title: Model answer: the Berlin Conference
cards.problem: (Exam question) Why was the Berlin Conference (1884–85) held and what did it decide?

steps.text: Problem: European powers, like Britain and Germany in East Africa, were rivals for African territory.
Meeting: the Berlin Conference was held in Germany in 1884–85, organised by Bismarck.
Aim: to stop conflicts among Europeans in Africa by setting rules for colonisation.
Rule: powers simply had to register their colonies with the Berlin office to get recognition – which sped up the partition of Africa.

cards.answer: Bismarck's Berlin Conference set rules (register your colony to have it recognised) to avoid European wars over Africa, and so accelerated its partition.

cards.title: South Africa
body: The Boers or Afrikaners were the first white settlers at the tip of South Africa before 1800s.
But after the Napoleonic wars British controlled it and encouraged settlers in what then called cape colony.
The Boers opposed and created their own cities the Transvaal and Orange Free State (South Africa.
In the interior the native blacks were organized under the Zulu under their leader SHAKA ZULU they entered in to several conflicts with the white supremacist the Boers.
Things started to change with coming of the famous successful business man Cecil Rhodes who controlled Rhodesia present day Zambia and Zimbabwe.

Both British and the Boers agreed to solve their differences and create South African under British colony with separated free gov’t led by only whites .in 1910 the south African republic gov’t was created.

cards.q: Southern Rhodesia was the former name for the present day of ______.
cards.why:
**Step 1:** From the lesson: “Cecil Rhodes controlled Rhodesia, present-day Zambia and Zimbabwe (Southern Rhodesia is now Zimbabwe).”

**Step 2:** **Step 1:** Identify the colonial names of Southern African countries.
**Step 2:** Northern Rhodesia became Zambia. Nyasaland became Malawi.
**Step 3:** Southern Rhodesia, named after Cecil Rhodes, became **Zimbabwe** after a long struggle for independence and majority rule in 1980.
**Result:** Zimbabwe.

**Step 3:** So the answer is B) Zimbabwe.

**Tip:** Underline the key word in the question (true / not / except / first / last), then test every option against the lesson facts and dates.

cards.title: Past exam (Model exam 2024)
cards.q: The Dutch settlers in south Africa were known as:
cards.why:
**Step 1:** From the lesson: “The Boers or Afrikaners were the first white settlers at the tip of South Africa before the 1800s.”

**Step 2:** **Step 1:** Identify the origin of European settlers in South Africa.
**Step 2:** The Dutch East India Company established a station at the Cape in 1652.
**Step 3:** These Dutch farmers and their descendants became known as 'Boers' (the Dutch word for farmers).
**Step 4:** They later developed the Afrikaans language and were called Afrikaners.
**Result:** Boers.

**Step 3:** So the answer is B) Boers.

**Tip:** Underline the key word in the question (true / not / except / first / last), then test every option against the lesson facts and dates.

cards.title: Model answer: South Africa under colonialism
cards.problem: (Short answer) Describe the colonisation of South Africa up to 1910.

steps.text: Boers: the Boers (Afrikaners) were the first white settlers at the Cape before the 1800s.
British: after the Napoleonic wars Britain took the Cape Colony; the Boers left and founded the Transvaal and Orange Free State.
African resistance: the Zulu under Shaka Zulu fought the Boers; Cecil Rhodes controlled Rhodesia (Zambia and Zimbabwe).
Union: Britain and the Boers settled their differences, and in 1910 a white-only South African government was created under the British.

cards.answer: Boer settlers, then the British, colonised South Africa, fighting the Zulu; in 1910 they united in a white-ruled South Africa under Britain.

cards.title: Nature of the colonial rule
body: By allowing the local chiefs to continue their former power British was well- known for the usage of indirect rule in Africa.

In its vast colonial empire in Africa France was well for using policy of assimilation and direct rule. Assimilation allowed the native people to participate in lower ranks of gov’t in expense of their truly identity.

cards.title: Model answer: indirect rule vs assimilation
cards.problem: (Exam question) Compare British and French methods of colonial rule in Africa.

steps.text: Britain – indirect rule: local chiefs kept their former power and ruled under British supervision.
France – direct rule and assimilation: French officials ruled directly.
Assimilation meant: Africans could join the lower ranks of government if they adopted French culture, losing their true identity.
Similarity: both served the colonial power's interests.

cards.answer: Britain ruled indirectly through chiefs; France ruled directly and tried to assimilate Africans into French culture, at the cost of their identity.
